about: Canadian financial technology company offering consumer investing, trading, crypto, tax filing, chequing and savings accounts and managed portfolios through the Wealthsimple app. Targets mainly younger Canadians, with over 3 million clients and tens of billions of Canadian dollars in assets. Headquartered in Toronto; launched 2014 as part of Power Corporation's group. Private, valued at 10 billion Canadian dollars after a 2025 funding round. Strong Canadian consumer brand with heavy advertising, previous sports and team partnerships.

wiki.title: Wealthsimple
wiki.text: Wealthsimple Inc. is a Canadian online investment management service. The firm was founded in September 2014 by Michael Katchen, Brett Huneycutt, and Rudy Adler and is based in Toronto. As of November 5, 2025, the firm holds over C$170 billion in assets under administration. It is primarily owned by Power Corporation, which holds a 52.4% undiluted stake aggregated through three entities: its wholly-owned subsidiary, its majority-owned subsidiary, and its controlled alternative asset platform.

about: Australian buy now pay later fintech giving consumers instalment credit through Zip Pay and Zip Money at online and in-store retailers in Australia, New Zealand and, importantly, the United States, where it is the main growth market. Earns merchant and customer fees, with millions of users and thousands of merchants. Headquartered in Sydney; founded 2013. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ZIP). Recognised consumer finance brand in Australia and growing in the US, and has used sports partnerships.

FalconX is a digital asset prime broker offering trading, lending, custody and derivatives for crypto institutions such as funds, banks and miners, and acquired 21Shares in 2025. Founded 2018 by Raghu Yarlagadda and based in San Mateo, California. Raised about 1.5 billion dollars in funding and valued at 8 billion dollars. Privately held. Institutional B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

ID Finance is a Spanish fintech lender using machine learning to offer online consumer loans and credit cards in Spain, Mexico, Brazil, Poland and the Philippines, through brands such as MoneyMan and Creditea. Customers are retail borrowers who apply by app. Headquartered in Barcelona; founded 2012. Private, with funding of about 900 million dollars including debt. Active marketing in consumer finance but little general brand recognition.
cb_desc: ID Finance is a fintech company offering lending, credit, fraud...

wiki.title: ID Finance
wiki.text: ID Finance is a financial technology company founded in 2012 by Boris Batine and Alexander Dunaev. It is predominantly focused on emerging markets, which are characterized by noncompetitive financial services, limited availability of credit and high barriers to entry.

about: CleanSpark is a US bitcoin miner that runs mining data centers in Georgia, Tennessee and Wyoming and has been expanding into AI and high-performance computing, with a strategy of owning its sites and power. Headquartered in Henderson, Nevada (input) and listed on Nasdaq (CLSK). Earnings track bitcoin prices and hashrate. Little mass consumer awareness, but known to crypto investors, with sponsorship deals in sports.

Fiserv is a financial technology provider offering core banking processing, payments (Clover merchant platform, First Data), digital banking and card issuing to banks, credit unions and merchants. Revenue near 20 billion dollars with about 38,000 employees. Headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; founded 1984. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FI, now FISV). Fiserv's stock dropped heavily in 2025 on weaker guidance. B2B brand, recognised via Fiserv Forum naming rights for the Milwaukee Bucks arena.

wiki.title: Fiserv
wiki.what: Provider of financial services technology to banks
wiki.text: Fiserv, Inc. is an American multinational financial technology company headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The company processes debit and credit card transactions, loyalty programs, loans, electronic bill pay, wires and ACH transfers, check deposits, and ATM transactions on behalf of banking institutions. The company also produces debit and credit cards and point of sale terminals.

about: FNZ is a wealth management platform provider that supplies technology and operations to banks, insurers and asset managers, administering investment accounts for millions of end customers in many countries. Headquartered in London with roots in New Zealand; founded 2003. Privately held, with investors including Generation Investment Management, CDPQ and Oakley; employees hold stakes. Valued at about 20 billion dollars in 2022 and recapitalised later. B2B finance brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: FNZ (company)
wiki.text: FNZ is a global financial services company that provides investment platforms to major financial institutions and wealth management firms. As of March 2025, FNZ manages over US$2 trillion in assets. FNZ's technology platform provides services such as investment front office, tax wrappers and investment back office.

about: AvidXchange provides accounts payable automation and payment software for mid-market businesses in the US, handling invoices, approvals and payments, and a network of suppliers. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina; founded 2000. Listed on Nasdaq (AVDX) in 2021 and taken private by TPG in 2025 in a deal valued at about 2.2 billion dollars. B2B brand with no consumer awareness, though it had sponsored sports and naming rights in Charlotte.

Nakamoto Holdings is a Utah-based company created by David Bailey's Nakamoto bitcoin treasury strategy through a 2025 merger with healthcare company KindlyMD (Murray, Utah), which holds a large bitcoin balance and plans to buy more. Listed on Nasdaq (NAKA). Funding shown is about 965 million dollars. Investor-focused brand, with no wider consumer recognition.
cb_desc: Kindly MD Company is designed to serve as a global..

wiki.title: Nakamoto
wiki.text: Nakamoto is a Japanese surname. Notable people with the surname include:Himeka Nakamoto, Japanese mental health counselor, former idol and former member of Nogizaka46 Hiroshi Nakamoto, Japanese baseball player Katsuya Nakamoto , Japanese freestyle skier Kentaro Nakamoto, Japanese long distance runner Kōji Nakamoto , Japanese comedian Kuniharu Nakamoto, Japanese football player Lynn Nakamoto, Japanese American judge Miriam Nakamoto, Japanese American Muay Thai fighter Mitsuaki Nakamoto, Japanese handball player in the 1984 Olympics Satoshi Nakamoto, the pseudonymous creator of the bitcoin digital currency Shuhei Nakamoto, vice-president of Hon

about: Altavair is described by Crunchbase as an asset management firm focused on finance and financial services, headquartered in Issaquah, Washington. The input lists finance and financial services as its industries and shows funding of about $2.4bn with the latest round in June 2026. The exact asset classes, clients and ownership are not given in the input. Likely a specialised asset or lease finance business, but unconfirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Altavair is an asset management firm focused..

about: Bilt is a New York rewards and payments company that lets renters earn points on rent payments through the Bilt Mastercard, which has no fee for paying rent, and redeem them for travel, home and other rewards. It has over a million members and a $10.75bn valuation after a 2025 raise. Founded by Ankur Jain, with investors including General Catalyst, Valor and Left Lane. Private. Strong awareness among US renters and credit card enthusiasts.

LPL Financial is the largest independent broker-dealer in the US, headquartered in San Diego, Boston and Fort Mill, supporting more than 22,000 financial advisors with brokerage, advisory, custody, research and technology platforms, and about $1.7 trillion in client assets. Revenue is above $10bn. Listed on Nasdaq (LPLA). Advisor-facing brand, advertised to retail investors through its Independent firms, with moderate awareness.

wiki.title: LPL Financial
wiki.what: Independent broker-dealer in the United States
wiki.text: LPL Financial Holdings Inc. was founded in 1989 and has been described as the largest independent broker-dealer in the United States. As of 2026, the company had more than 32,000 financial advisors, approximately US$2.3 trillion in client assets, including US$1.4 trillion in advisory assets. LPL Financial has main offices in Boston, Fort Mill, Austin, and San Diego. The company is a member of FINRA and the SIPC.

about: LMAX Group is a London-based financial technology company operating electronic trading venues, including LMAX Exchange for institutional foreign exchange, LMAX Digital for cryptocurrency trading, and FX Clearing. Founded around 2010, it serves brokers, banks, hedge funds and other institutions and earns trading, clearing and technology fees. Regulated in the UK and privately held. B2B finance brand, known in trading circles and with little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: LMAX Group is an independent financial technology company..

wiki.title: LMAX Group
wiki.text: LMAX Group is a financial betting company based in London, UK.

about: Invesco is an Atlanta, Georgia-based independent global investment manager with about $1.9 trillion of assets under management, offering active and passive funds including the Invesco QQQ ETF and the former PowerShares range. It serves retail and institutional investors in over 20 countries. Listed on NYSE (IVZ). Investor brand known in finance, with stadium naming and sports sponsorship history such as Invesco Field.

wiki.title: Invesco
wiki.text: Invesco Ltd., organized in Bermuda, with principal executive offices in Atlanta, Georgia, is an investment management company. The company has clients in 120 countries.

about: Melio is a New York-based fintech with large operations in Israel, offering a digital accounts payable and receivable platform that lets small businesses pay vendors by bank transfer or card. Founded in 2018 by Matan Bar and Ilan Atias, it had raised about $654 million. Xero acquired it for $2.5 billion in 2025. Customers are US small businesses and accountants. B2B fintech, low consumer awareness.

Plasma is a UK-based blockchain project (a Layer 1 network) focused on stablecoin payments and real-time settlement, reported to be backed by Tether and Paolo Ardoino. The input shows reported funding of about $397 million, with a base in London. It launched its mainnet in 2025. B2B crypto infrastructure with awareness mainly among crypto users. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Plasma is an operational setting that supports payments, real-..

about: Rapyd is a fintech-as-a-service company that provides payment acceptance, cross-border payouts, wallets and card issuing through one API, used by merchants and platforms in many countries. Headquartered in London with large operations in Israel, it was founded in 2016 and reached a 15 billion dollar valuation in 2021 before cutting it. It acquired PayU's global payments business in 2023. Customers are online platforms and businesses. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Rapyd
wiki.text: Rapyd is a digital payment processing and fintech services company founded in Tel Aviv in 2016. The company provides a platform for payments and financial services. It is Israel's largest private high-tech company.

about: StoneX Group is a US financial services firm headquartered in New York and listed on Nasdaq (SNEX). It provides execution, clearing, market-making, physical commodities, FX and international payments services to commercial hedgers, institutions and retail traders across more than 80 countries, with about 4,500 employees. Formerly INTL FCStone, renamed in 2020. Customers are corporates, banks and traders. B2B financial brand known in markets, not to mass consumers.

wiki.title: StoneX Group Inc.
wiki.text: StoneX Group Inc. is an American financial services company. The company operates in six areas: commercial hedging, global payments, securities, physical commodities, foreign exchange and clearing and execution services (CES).

about: Aria is a Paris-based financial technology company that, according to its Crunchbase listing, develops payment-related products. Customers, ownership, products and scale are not confirmed from the input. Several companies share this name, so verify before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Aria is a FinTech company that develops payment....

wiki.title: Aria
wiki.what: Musical piece for a single voice as part of a larger work
wiki.text: In music, an aria is a self-contained piece for one voice, with or without instrumental or orchestral accompaniment, normally part of a larger work.

about: Flow Traders is an Amsterdam-based technology-driven liquidity provider and market maker, trading exchange-traded products (ETFs and ETPs), equities, fixed income and crypto assets on global venues. Customers are exchanges, issuers and institutions, with revenue from trading gains and spreads of several hundred million euros. Founded in 2004. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (FLOW). B2B, with low retail awareness.

wiki.title: Flow Traders
wiki.text: Flow Traders is a proprietary trading firm. A market maker, it provides liquidity in the securities market by using high frequency and quantitative trading strategies.

about: Flowdesk is a Paris-based digital asset trading company providing market making, liquidity, over-the-counter trading and treasury services to crypto projects, exchanges and institutions, using algorithmic strategies. Founded in 2020. Customers are token issuers and exchanges. Crunchbase shows about $282 million in funding, which likely includes capital for trading. Private. B2B brand known in the crypto industry, with no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Flowdesk is a digital assethi trading company that combin...

about: New York-based institutional crypto trading platform, founded 2018, offering order management and trading infrastructure to banks, brokers and asset managers. Raised around $196 million. B2B with low consumer awareness. Customers include banks and hedge funds, which pay platform and trading fees. B2B brand with no consumer awareness; known among institutional crypto traders. Talos provides a trading platform with access to many liquidity venues, including spot, derivatives and decentralised finance.

wiki.title: Talos
wiki.text: In Greek mythology, Talos, also spelled Talus or Talon, was a man of bronze who protected Crete from pirates and invaders. Despite the popular idea that he was a giant, no ancient source states this explicitly.

about: Pipe is a San Francisco fintech platform that lets companies with recurring revenue, such as subscription software businesses, sell future revenue streams for upfront capital, and trade them with investors. Founded in 2019, it has raised about 450 million dollars in equity and debt from investors including Greenspring, Shopify and others. B2B financial platform with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Pipe (company)
wiki.text: Pipe was a Belgian automobile manufacturer founded by the brothers Alfred and Victor Goldschmidt. The company was also known as Compagnie Belge de Construction Automobiles.

about: CME Group is the Chicago-based operator of the world's largest derivatives exchanges, including the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX, trading futures and options on interest rates, equities, energy, metals, agriculture and foreign exchange. It is listed on Nasdaq (CME), has revenue of over 6 billion dollars and also provides clearing. Customers are institutional traders and hedgers. Respected in finance but with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: CME Group
wiki.text: CME Group Inc., headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, operates exchanges and provides clearing services for trading in financial derivatives such as futures contracts, options, and swaps. Its exchanges include the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), and the Commodity Exchange (COMEX). The company also owns 27% of S&P Dow Jones Indices. The company operates the Globex Trading System, an electronic trading platform that allows customers in approximately 150 countries to trade futures and options contracts. The company also operates two platforms for spot market trading: B

about: Blockstream is a bitcoin and blockchain technology company, founded in 2014 by Adam Back and based in Menlo Park, California, with operations worldwide. It builds Liquid sidechain, Bitcoin mining facilities and the Jade hardware wallet and satellite broadcast. Customers are exchanges, miners and individual users. It has raised about $632 million. Well-known in the bitcoin community, with limited mainstream awareness.

wiki.title: Blockstream
wiki.text: Blockstream is a blockchain technology company co-founded by Adam Back in 2014. The company develops infrastructure for the Bitcoin network, including sidechains, privacy enhancements, and tools for both institutional and consumer use. It is known for its contributions to Bitcoin protocol development and its suite of Bitcoin-native financial products and services. Blockstream is headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in Lugano and Tokyo.

about: South Korean cryptocurrency exchange based in Seoul, one of the country's largest by volume, providing trading in bitcoin, ethereum and other tokens to retail users. Founded 2014. Reported funding about USD 233 million. Regulated by Korean authorities; Korbit and other rivals compete. Consumer fintech brand with solid domestic awareness and advertising presence.

Copper is a London-based digital asset custody and technology firm, founded in 2018, providing institutional crypto custody, prime brokerage and settlement networks (ClearLoop) for funds and exchanges. Customers are institutions. Crunchbase shows about $281 million in funding. Founder Dmitry Tokarev leads the company. B2B crypto infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Copper
wiki.text: Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu and atomic number 29. It is a soft, malleable, and ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity. A freshly exposed surface of pure copper has a pinkish-orange color. Copper is used as a conductor of heat and electricity, as a building material, and as a constituent of various metal alloys, such as sterling silver used in jewelry, cupronickel used to make marine hardware and coins, and constantan used in strain gauges and thermocouples for temperature measurement.

about: HashKey Group is a Hong Kong digital asset financial services group, led by Xiao Feng, which operates the licensed HashKey Exchange, asset management, and the HashKey Chain, and has been seeking a Hong Kong listing. It has raised about $130 million. Customers are retail and institutional crypto investors. Prominent in the Hong Kong crypto sector, with limited broad public awareness.

Grayscale Investments is a Stamford, Connecticut digital currency asset manager, which offers investment trusts and ETFs providing exposure to Bitcoin, Ethereum and other cryptocurrencies, including the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust (GBTC) converted into an ETF in January 2024. It is a subsidiary of Digital Currency Group, founded by Barry Silbert, and manages tens of billions of dollars of assets. It earns management fees. It is well known to crypto investors and advertises in finance media.

wiki.title: Grayscale
wiki.what: Digital image having no color information
wiki.text: In digital photography, computer-generated imagery, and colorimetry, a grayscale or greyscale image is one in which the value of each pixel holds no color information. Pixel values are typically stored in the range 0 to 255.

about: 360 ONE Wealth (formerly IIFL Wealth Management) is an Indian wealth and asset management firm based in Mumbai that serves high-net-worth families and entrepreneurs with wealth management, investment, lending and asset management services. It manages assets worth around 5 trillion rupees and is listed on the NSE and BSE (360ONE). Backed by General Atlantic and others. Premium financial brand known to wealthy Indians, with sports sponsorship in cricket.

XTransfer is a Chinese cross-border B2B payments and risk control fintech based in Shanghai, helping small and medium-sized exporters and importers receive and send international payments, with compliance and risk management services. It serves hundreds of thousands of small businesses trading with China and has raised about 248 million dollars, with investors including Tiger Global and Sequoia China. B2B, with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: XTransfer
wiki.text: XTransfer, registered in Hong Kong as XTransfer Ltd., is a Chinese fintech company founded in May 2017. Headquartered in Shanghai, it focuses on providing SMEs with cross-border financial services. The company also offers risk management and banking compliance services. It serves enterprises within and outside China. As of March 2022, its valuation reached $1 billion.

about: Xendit is an Indonesian payments infrastructure fintech, founded in 2015 and based in Jakarta, which provides payment gateways, disbursements and business accounts for companies across Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia. Customers include merchants and platforms. Founders Moses Lo and Zac Ong started Xendit. B2B with low consumer profile.

BILL (formerly Bill.com) is a US financial automation software company headquartered in San Jose, California and listed on the NYSE (BILL). It provides accounts payable, receivable and spend management tools, including Divvy corporate cards and Invoice2go, to over 400,000 small and mid-sized businesses and accounting firms, with revenue near 1.4 billion dollars. Founded 2006. Customers pay subscription, interchange and transaction fees. B2B brand well known among US accountants and small businesses.

wiki.title: Bill.com
wiki.text: BILL Holdings, Inc. is an American company based in San Jose, California, that provides automated, cloud-based software for financial operations for small businesses in the United States. A white-labeled, end-to-end payments automation platform, Bill.com Connect is offered to financial institutions as part of their single sign-on online business banking ecosystem.

about: Papaya Global is an Israeli-American workforce payments and global payroll platform, founded in 2016 and now headquartered in New York, that manages payroll and payments for companies employing people in 160 countries. Customers are mid-size and global enterprises, paid by subscription. Backed by Workday Ventures, Tiger Global and others. B2B brand known among HR teams.

wiki.title: Papaya Global
wiki.text: Papaya Global is a fintech SaaS company that specializes in global workforce payroll and payments. Eynat Guez is the CEO and co-founder of the company. The company gained unicorn status in 2021. In March 2022, Papaya Global acquired Azimo. The company provides a unified platform that enables businesses to pay and manage employees and contractors worldwide, ensuring compliance with local regulations. Initially, Papaya has expanded into a payments-first workforce management platform, supporting organizations in over 160 countries.

about: NYDIG (New York Digital Investment Group) is a bitcoin-focused financial firm offering institutional custody, trading, lending, mining and bitcoin-enabled banking services, and managing funds. It enables community banks and fintechs to offer bitcoin to their customers. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York, it is majority owned by Stone Ridge Holdings, with strategic investment from banks and financial partners such as Mass Mutual, Soros Fund Management and Bessemer. B2B and institutional-facing; modest public brand awareness outside finance and crypto circles.

Pleo is a Danish fintech company providing company cards, expense management and spend control for small and medium businesses in Europe. Employees receive smart cards with spending limits, and receipts are automatically matched. Founded in 2015 in Copenhagen, it has raised about 470 million dollars from Kinnevik, Creandum, Founders Fund and others, and has tens of thousands of customers in Denmark, Sweden, Germany, the UK and Ireland. B2B fintech with solid brand recognition among European SMEs.

wiki.title: Pleo
wiki.text: PLEO is an animatronic pet dinosaur toy manufactured by Innvo Labs, a company located in both Hong Kong and Nevada. The toy has the appearance and (imagined) behavior of a week-old baby Camarasaurus dinosaur. It was designed by Caleb Chung, the co-creator of the Furby, Chung's company Ugobe first sold Pleo and was manufactured by Jetta Company Limited. The species of dinosaur chosen allows for concealing the sensors and motors needed for the animation, since it has a big body shape and relatively large head. According to their website, each Pleo would "learn" from its experiences and environment through artificial intelligence and develop an

about: Matter Labs is a Berlin-based blockchain company, founded in 2018 by Alex Gluchowski, that develops zkSync, an Ethereum layer-2 network that uses zero-knowledge proofs for scaling, and the ZK token. It raised about 458 million dollars from a16z, Dragonfly, Blockchain Capital and others. Customers are developers and applications on the network. Known in crypto, minimal consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Matter Labs is a blockchain technology company focused...

about: Verifone is one of the world's largest makers of point-of-sale payment terminals, offering card readers, countertop and mobile terminals, the Carbon smart-POS line, and payment software, gateway and processing services for merchants. Customers are retailers, restaurants, banks, acquirers and fuel and transport operators in over 150 countries, paid through hardware sales and recurring software and services fees. Founded in 1981, it is privately held after the 2018 take-private by Francisco Partners and was later restructured, with Griffin Investment Partners among later owners. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness beyond seeing its terminals at checkouts.

wiki.title: Verifone
wiki.text: Verifone, Inc. is an American multinational corporation headquartered in New York City. Verifone provides technology for electronic payment transactions and value-added services at the point of sale (POS). Verifone sells merchant-operated, consumer-facing and self-service payment systems to the financial, retail, hospitality, petroleum, government and healthcare industries. The company's products consist of POS electronic payment devices that run its own operating systems, security and encryption software, and certified payment software, and that are designed for both consumer-facing and unattended environments.

about: Ethic is a New York-based investment technology firm providing a platform for wealth advisers to build and manage portfolios that follow clients' values, such as sustainable and impact investing, with direct indexing and tax-aware management. Founded in 2016 by Dave Wolfe, it has raised about $163 million. Customers are financial advisers, wealth managers and individual investors, with revenue from advisory fees. Moderate recognition within the impact investing community.
cb_desc: Ethic develops technology that helps wealth advisors.

wiki.title: Ethics
wiki.text: Ethics is the philosophical study of moral phenomena. Also called moral philosophy, it investigates normative questions about what people ought to do or which behavior is morally right. Its main branches include normative ethics, applied ethics, and metaethics.

about: Bitso is a Mexico City-based cryptocurrency exchange, founded in 2014, and one of the largest in Latin America. It lets consumers and businesses buy, sell and send crypto and stablecoins, with strong remittance flows between the US and Mexico, and operates in Mexico, Argentina, Brazil and Colombia. It makes money from trading spreads and fees, and has millions of users. Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Tiger Global and Paradigm, and a known consumer brand in Mexico, including football sponsorship deals.

Lightspark is a Los Angeles-based payments infrastructure company, founded in 2022 by former Facebook Libra and Diem executive David Marcus, that builds on the Bitcoin Lightning Network to enable fast, low-cost global payments for digital banks, wallets, exchanges and enterprises. It offers APIs and a payment network layer and earns fees from transactions. It raised about $175 million from investors including a16z, Ribbit Capital and Paradigm. B2B fintech and crypto brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Lightspark
wiki.what: Free and open source SWF player
wiki.text: Lightspark is a free and open-source Adobe Flash (SWF) player released under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL) version 3.

wiki.title: David A. Marcus
wiki.text: David A. Marcus is a French-born American entrepreneur. He was the co-creator of Diem, a cryptocurrency project initiated by Facebook. He is the former president of PayPal and Vice President of Messaging Products at Facebook where he ran the Facebook Messenger unit from 2014 until 2018. In December 2017, Marcus was appointed to the Coinbase Board of Directors, from which he stepped down in 2018. In 2021, he stepped down from Facebook. As of May 2022 he is the co-founder and CEO of Lightspark, a cryptocurrency startup which works on bitcoin and the Lightning Network.

about: Magic Eden is an online marketplace for non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and digital collectibles, founded in 2021 on the Solana blockchain and expanded to Ethereum, Bitcoin Ordinals and other chains, with a crypto wallet and a gaming focus. It earns marketplace fees on trades and has millions of users. It has raised about $170 million, at a valuation of $1.6 billion in 2022, and is headquartered in San Francisco. Well known in crypto communities, with ambassador and sports sponsorship activity.

Blockdaemon is a Los Angeles-based provider of institutional blockchain infrastructure, offering node hosting, staking, APIs and wallet services for networks such as Ethereum, Solana and Bitcoin. Customers include exchanges, banks, wallets and asset managers, who pay usage and staking fees. It raised about $431 million and was valued at $3.25 billion in 2022. Founded in 2017. B2B crypto brand known within the blockchain industry, with no consumer recognition.

BGC Group is a New York-based financial brokerage and technology company, listed on Nasdaq (BGC), affiliated with Cantor Fitzgerald and led by Howard Lutnick, that brokers fixed income, foreign exchange, equities, energy and commodities for institutional clients, and runs Fenics electronic trading platforms. It has roughly 4,000 employees and revenue of around $2.2 billion. Its customers are banks, hedge funds and large corporations. B2B financial brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: BGC Group
wiki.text: BGC Group, Inc. is an American global financial services company based in New York City and London. Originally formed as part of the larger Cantor Fitzgerald organization, BGC Partners became its own entity in 2004.

about: San Francisco payments company offering a full-stack payment processing platform for software companies and marketplaces that want to embed payments, handling onboarding, processing and settlement. Customers are vertical SaaS firms; revenue from per-transaction fees. Founded in 2015, venture-funded with about $201 million. B2B fintech brand.
cb_desc: Finix is a full-stack payment processor that develops a...

about: US financial advisory firm in New York offering M&A, restructuring and capital advisory services. Founded in 2006 by Joseph Perella and Peter Weinberg, both veteran Wall Street dealmakers, it works for corporates, boards and institutions, earning advisory and success fees, with offices in the US, Europe and beyond. Listed on Nasdaq (PWP) since going public through a SPAC in 2021. Revenue is in the high hundreds of millions of dollars. Premium B2B brand.

Wealthfront is a Palo Alto, California robo-advisor and financial app offering automated investing, high-yield cash accounts, bond ladders, stock portfolio tools and borrowing to millions of mostly young US customers. Founded in 2008, it manages tens of billions of dollars and raised about 274 million dollars. UBS had agreed to buy it in 2022 but canceled the deal, and it filed for a Nasdaq IPO in late 2025 (WLTH). Well-known fintech consumer brand in the US.

wiki.title: Wealthfront
wiki.text: Wealthfront Corporation is an American financial services company based in Palo Alto, California, founded by Andy Rachleff and Dan Carroll in 2008. As of September 2026, Wealthfront reported approximately $100 billion assets under management for more than 1.5 million clients.

about: Redpin is a London-based financial services firm and fintech, whose description is that it connects global citizens and businesses by simplifying cross-border payments and banking. Funding shown is about 140 million. Customers are individuals and companies needing international payments, but its products, ownership and scale are not confirmed from the input. Low public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Redpin connect globalcitizens and businesses by simplifying..

about: ThetaRay is a financial crime detection company, headquartered in New York with research in Israel, whose AI-based platform detects money laundering and fraud in cross-border payments, for banks and payments firms. Customers include Mastercard and other banks and fintechs across the world. Founded in 2013, it raised about 170 million dollars. Private. B2B, known in compliance circles, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: ThetaRay
wiki.what: Cyber security and data analytics company
wiki.text: ThetaRay is a fintech software and big data analytics company with headquarters in Hod HaSharon, Israel and New York, and offices in Madrid, London, and Singapore.

about: TheStreet is a New York-based financial news and information company, founded in 1996 by Jim Cramer. It publishes market news, stock analysis, investing advice and personal-finance content via TheStreet.com and sells premium subscriptions and ad-supported content. It was listed on Nasdaq (TST) until it was acquired by TheMaven (now Arena Group) in 2019, and it later sold its Ratings business and was further divested. Known name among US retail investors.

wiki.title: TheStreet
wiki.what: US financial news and financial literacy website
wiki.text: TheStreet is a financial news and financial literacy website. It is a subsidiary of The Arena Group. The company provides both free content and subscription services such as TheStreet Pro, a stock recommendation portfolio managed by Chris Versace. TheStreet was founded by Marty Peretz and Jim Cramer, and the site boasted numerous notable former contributors, including Aaron Task, Herb Greenberg, and Brett Arends.

about: CoinShares is a European digital asset investment firm based in St Helier, Jersey, which runs exchange-traded products (including Physical Bitcoin, listed in Europe), actively managed funds, a trading and capital markets desk and staking services. Customers are institutional and retail investors, and revenue is management fees and trading income, with assets under management of several billion dollars. It listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and added a US Nasdaq listing in 2025 (CSHR). Known in crypto finance circles, with growing profile.

wiki.title: CoinShares International
wiki.text: CoinShares International Limited is a financial services provider and asset manager based in Jersey that specializes in digital assets. The company, headquartered in St. Helier (Jersey), was founded in 2013 / 2014 and is considered one of the first companies in the crypto investment sector. CoinShares offers institutional and private investors access to crypto investments, for example through exchange-traded crypto products (ETPs), funds, and other financial products. The group has been listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange since 2021, and in September 2025, a secondary listing on the New York Stock Exchange was announced.

about: Billtrust is a US software company, based in Lawrenceville, New Jersey (listed in Nashville, Tennessee), that supplies accounts receivable automation, invoicing and payments software to B2B companies. It listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2021 (BTRS) and was taken private by EQT in early 2022 for around $1.7 billion. Customers include thousands of mid-market and enterprise suppliers. B2B fintech brand with no consumer visibility.

Modulr is a London-based payments company offering account and payments infrastructure through APIs, so that businesses and software platforms can embed payments, accounts and collections into their products. It is authorised by the UK's Financial Conduct Authority as an e-money institution, and serves fintechs, payroll and marketplace platforms and corporates. It earns on transaction fees and platform charges. Founded in 2015, it has raised about 145 million, including a Series C in 2022 led by General Atlantic. Privately held. B2B, little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Modulr is on a mission to unlock the embedded payment...

about: Mercer Advisors is a Denver, Colorado wealth management firm and one of the largest registered investment advisers in the United States, offering financial planning, investment management, tax and estate services to affluent families and retirees. It has grown by acquiring dozens of independent advisory firms, and manages well over $100 billion in client assets. It is backed by private equity investors and earns advisory fees. Regional and referral-based brand, with modest awareness among the general public.
cb_desc: Mercer Advisors is a full-service wealth management firm.

about: CI Financial is a Toronto-based wealth and asset management company offering mutual funds, advisory and wealth services in Canada, the US and Australia through CI Global Asset Management, Corient and others, with hundreds of billions of dollars under management and administration. Customers are retail investors and advisors, with revenue from management fees. Taken private in 2025 by a Mubadala Capital-led investor group, previously listed on the TSX (CIX). Known among Canadian investors.

wiki.title: CI Financial
wiki.text: CI Financial is a Canadian investment management company based in Toronto, Ontario. It offers investment management and wealth management services targeted to high net worth retail investors, as well as brokerage and trading services to portfolio managers and institutional investors.

about: Sanctuary Wealth is a US wealth management platform that lets established financial advisers and teams run independent, branded firms with shared technology, custody, compliance and investment support, in a partnership model. Revenue comes from advisory fees on assets supported by the platform. Based in Indianapolis according to Crunchbase, with a wide national network, it shows about $175 million in funding, with a round in July 2022. Privately held. Known in the adviser community, with limited awareness among individual investors.
cb_desc: Sanctuary Wealth is a financial services industry.

about: Decentralized finance company behind the 1inch Network, a suite of crypto products including a DEX aggregator that finds the best prices across exchanges, a liquidity protocol, a wallet, and a limit order and cross-chain swap system. Launched in 2019 by Sergej Kunz and Anton Bukov, it is incorporated in Saint Kitts and Nevis and run through a distributed team, and has its own 1INCH token. Revenue comes from swap fees. Customers are crypto traders. High awareness in the crypto community, and a sponsor in blockchain and sporting events.

Forgent is a Dayton, Minnesota-based designer and manufacturer of electrical distribution equipment for data centres and industrial customers, per the input, with funding of about $5 billion shown, which suggests a large private-equity or growth investment. B2B with no consumer awareness. The business was formerly private and is linked to US data centre electrical buildouts. The input shows funding of about $5 billion and does not give customer names or ownership. Its scale and public visibility should be checked.
cb_desc: A designer and manufacturer of electrical distribution....

wiki.title: Forgent
wiki.text: Forgent plc, formerly known as REACT Energy plc, EQTEC plc, and Kedco plc, is a bioscience energy company operating in the United Kingdom and Ireland which was established in 2005.

about: Verallia is a French glass packaging company, headquartered in Courbevoie, making bottles and jars for wine, spirits, beer and food and supplying producers in Europe, Latin America and the US, with about 30 plants and revenue of around 3.5 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (VRLA). B2B, little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Verallia is a global glassmaking player providing innovative an...

about: Dover Corporation is a US diversified industrial manufacturer headquartered in Downers Grove, Illinois, with five segments: engineered products, clean energy and fueling, imaging and identification, pumps and process solutions, and climate and sustainability technologies. Products include fuel dispensers (Wayne), fluid pumps, refrigeration cases, marking and coding equipment and vehicle service lifts. Customers are industrial, retail and energy businesses. Founded in 1955, listed on the NYSE (DOV), with revenue around 8 billion dollars. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Dover
wiki.what: Town and port in Kent, England
wiki.text: Dover is a town, major ferry port and civil parish in Kent, England. It faces France across the Strait of Dover, the narrowest part of the English Channel at 33 kilometres (21 mi) from Cap Gris-Nez in France. It lies southeast of Canterbury and east of Maidstone. The town is the administrative centre of the Dover District and home of the Port of Dover. In 2024 it had an estimated population of 44,209.

about: Ardagh Group is a global manufacturer of metal and glass packaging, supplying beverage cans, glass bottles and jars to drinks and food brands. Customers include major brewers, soft drink companies, wine and spirits makers and food producers across Europe, North America and Brazil. Headquartered in Luxembourg and controlled by the Paul Coulson family, it split into Ardagh Glass Packaging and Ardagh Metal Packaging (NYSE: AMBP). Revenue is around 9 billion dollars with about 23,000 employees. B2B supplier whose products are well known on shelves but whose name has little consumer recognition.

wiki.title: Ardagh Group
wiki.what: Luxembourg-based producer of glass and metal products
wiki.text: Ardagh Group is a producer of glass and metal products founded in Ireland and now based in Luxembourg, which has "grown in the past two decades into one of the world’s largest metal and glass packaging companies".

about: Enerpac Tool Group is a Milwaukee-based maker of high-pressure hydraulic tools and heavy-lifting equipment, including bolting and cutting tools, used in construction, energy, infrastructure and industrial maintenance, sold in more than 100 countries. Formerly part of Actuant, it is listed on the NYSE under EPAC with annual revenue around $600 million. Customers are industrial professionals. B2B tools brand with little consumer awareness.

ICON is an Austin, Texas construction technology company that 3D-prints homes and buildings using its Vulcan printers and CarbonX building material, with projects including community homes in Texas and the Wolf Ranch development, and work with NASA on lunar construction. Founded in 2017 by Jason Ballard and others, it has raised about $770 million. Customers are developers, nonprofits and governments. B2B with notable media attention, and some consumer curiosity.

wiki.title: Icon plc
wiki.text: Icon plc is an Irish-headquartered multinational clinical research organisation (CRO). Icon conducts clinical trials on behalf of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and provides services related to drug development and guiding clinical trial progress.

about: Allegro MicroSystems is a Manchester, New Hampshire semiconductor company, listed on Nasdaq (ALGM) and majority owned by Japan's Sanken Electric, that makes magnetic sensors and power ICs used in electric vehicles, ADAS, industrial automation and data centers. Customers are automakers and industrial manufacturers, with revenue of about $700-1,000 million. It has operations in the US, Philippines and Thailand. Established in 1936 as part of Sprague Electric. B2B chip supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Carbon is a Redwood City, California 3D printing company, founded in 2013 as Carbon3D, whose Digital Light Synthesis technology and printers produce production-quality polymer parts for manufacturers. Customers include Adidas (4D running shoe midsoles), dental labs, automotive and medical device companies, which buy printers on subscription plus resins. It has raised about $740 million and was valued at $2.5 billion in 2018. B2B industrial technology brand, known in manufacturing but less so with consumers.

wiki.title: Carbon
wiki.text: Carbon is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6. It is nonmetallic and tetravalent—meaning that its atoms are able to form up to four covalent bonds due to its valence shell exhibiting 4 electrons. It belongs to group 14 of the periodic table. Carbon makes up about 0.025 percent of Earth's crust. Three isotopes occur naturally, 12C and 13C being stable, while 14C is a radionuclide, decaying with a half-life of 5,700 years. Carbon is one of the few elements known since antiquity.

wiki.title: Carbon (company)
wiki.text: Carbon, Inc. is a digital manufacturing company that manufactures and develops 3D printers utilizing the Continuous Liquid Interface Production process. The company was founded in 2013, and maintains its headquarters in California, United States.

about: Velo3D is a Fremont, California-based metal 3D printing company, selling Sapphire laser powder bed fusion printers and software for aerospace, defence and energy parts. Listed via a SPAC in 2021, then delisted and later relisted on Nasdaq after restructuring; Arrayed Notes is its main shareholder. Customers include SpaceX and other aerospace names. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

ATS Corporation is a Cambridge, Ontario automation company (ATS Corp, TSX and NYSE: ATS) that designs and builds custom automation systems, such as assembly lines and test systems, for life sciences, transportation, food and consumer goods customers. It has about 7,000 employees and annual revenue of around 2 billion Canadian dollars. B2B engineering brand with no consumer recognition.

wiki.title: ATS Corporation
wiki.text: ATS Corporation is a Canadian company based in Cambridge, Ontario, that designs and builds factory automation systems. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

about: IMA Group is an Italian maker of automatic machines for packaging pharmaceuticals, tea, coffee, and cosmetics, based in Castenaso, near Bologna. Customers are pharmaceutical, food and beverage companies worldwide, and revenue is around 2 billion euros. Founded in 1961, it is controlled by Alberto Vacchi and BC Partners, which bought a major stake in 2020. B2B and in the Emilia-Romagna 'Packaging Valley' cluster, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Inverse Multiplexing for ATM
wiki.text: Inverse Multiplexing for ATM (IMA) is a standardized technology used to transport ATM traffic over a bundle of T1 or E1 lines, which is called an IMA Group. This allows for gradual increase in data link capacity where implementing a higher capacity solution like T3/E3 or SONET/SDH is not deemed feasible. The maximum number of lines in an IMA Group is 32, bringing the total data rate to roughly 64 Mbit/s. The standard specification was initially approved by The ATM Forum in July 1997, and was later updated to version 1.1 in March 1999.

about: FormFactor is a Livermore, California maker of advanced semiconductor wafer probe cards, analytical probes, probe stations, cryogenic systems and thermal test equipment used by chipmakers to test integrated circuits at the wafer level. Customers include memory and logic manufacturers such as SK hynix, Samsung and Intel, and revenue is around 700 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (FORM). B2B semiconductor equipment brand with no consumer awareness, so sponsorship appeal is limited to corporate hospitality.

wiki.title: FormFactor
wiki.text: FormFactor, Inc. is a provider of test and measurement technologies for integrated circuits, with its headquarters in Livermore, California. It provides semiconductor companies with products to improve device performance and provide test and measurement technologies for integrated circuits.

about: Photonic Inc. is a Coquitlam, British Columbia quantum technology company building a distributed, silicon-based quantum computing architecture linked by photons, founded in 2016, with strategic investors including Microsoft, with whom it has a partnership on quantum networking. It raised about 318 million dollars, and is privately held. Customers would be enterprises, governments and research bodies using future quantum computers. Research-stage technology brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Photonics
wiki.text: Photonics is a branch of optics that involves the application of generation, detection, and manipulation of light in the form of photons through emission, transmission, modulation, signal processing, switching, amplification, and sensing. Even though photonics is a commonly used term, there is no widespread agreement on a clear definition of the term or on the difference between photonics and related fields, such as optics.

about: Atomic Machines is an Emeryville, California deep-tech company developing atomic-scale manufacturing technology for MEMS, semiconductors and nano devices, with ambitions to build precise structures atom by atom. Recorded funding is about 250 million dollars, though this figure looks high for a startup at its stage. Customers would be chipmakers and advanced manufacturers. Privately held. Early-stage technology brand with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Amentum is a US government and critical infrastructure services contractor, based in Chantilly, Virginia, which merged with Jacobs' Critical Mission Solutions and Cyber & Intelligence businesses in September 2024 and now trades on the NYSE (AMTM). It provides engineering, technical and mission support to the US Department of Defense, NASA, the Department of Energy and allied governments, with revenue around $8-9 billion and about 53,000 employees. B2B brand with no consumer profile.

wiki.title: Amentum
wiki.what: Leather strap attached to a javelin used in ancient Greece
wiki.text: An amentum was a leather strap attached to a javelin used in ancient Greek athletics, hunting, and warfare, which helped to increase the range and the stability of the javelin in flight. Stability in flight was important because it allowed the javelin to land on its point, which was the only way the throw could be accurately recorded in competition or be useful against a live target. An amentum also increased the effective length of the throwing arm similarly to a spear-thrower or Swiss arrow, which enhances the speed of the projectile.

wiki.title: Amentum Holdings
wiki.text: Amentum Holdings, Inc. is an American government and commercial services contractor based in Chantilly, Virginia. The company was formed in 2020 from the spinout of AECOM's Management Services / federal group. After Leidos, it is the second-largest government services contractor in the US government contracting market.

about: AssetWatch is a Dublin, Ohio, condition monitoring company that sells wireless sensors and analytics for industrial machinery, alerting plant maintenance teams about faults such as bearing wear. Customers are manufacturers and process plants, paying monthly subscriptions. Founded in 2018, it raised about $166 million, including a 2025 round. B2B industrial IoT brand with no consumer awareness. Its subscription revenue is recurring, and it sells to plant managers and reliability engineers, so there is no consumer awareness and sponsorship relevance is limited.

SI Group is a global specialty chemicals manufacturer headquartered in The Woodlands, Texas, with roots in Schenectady, New York. It makes antioxidants, resins, intermediates and other additives used in plastics, rubber, fuels, coatings, adhesives and tyres, selling to industrial manufacturers worldwide. It operates plants and sites across North America, Europe and Asia and has thousands of employees. It is privately held with private-equity backing. Crunchbase shows $150 million of financing in late 2025. B2B only, with little consumer awareness, and limited sponsorship relevance.
cb_desc: SI Group is a developer and manufacturer of chemical...

about: OpenWeb, formerly Spot.IM, is a New York-based engagement and conversation platform with roots in Israel, founded in 2012. It provides comment sections, community tools and moderation technology to publishers such as Yahoo, AOL, Sky News and USA Today, and offers advertising tools that monetise those on-site conversations. Customers are publishers and brands. It is privately held and has raised about 393 million dollars. B2B media technology brand, well known in publishing, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: OpenWeb
wiki.text: OpenWeb is a social engagement platform that builds online communities around digital content. OpenWeb works with publishers to bring conversations back from social networks to publisher sites.

about: ARRIS, now Arris Composites, is a US advanced manufacturing company based in Berkeley, California, that developed additive moulding, a process for making complex continuous-fibre composite parts by moulding compressed fibre bundles. It makes lightweight carbon-fibre components for aerospace, automotive, medical and consumer products, selling parts and licences to manufacturers. It is venture backed and has raised about 239 million dollars. B2B materials technology brand with little public awareness.
cb_desc: ARRIS develops an additive molding technology for...

wiki.title: Arris International
wiki.text: Arris International Limited was an American telecommunications equipment company engaged in data, video and telephony systems for homes and businesses.

about: Glaston is a Finnish technology company making glass processing machines, especially for tempering, laminating and bending architectural, automotive and appliance glass, and offers upgrades, spare parts and service plus software. Its customers are glass processors serving construction, automotive and solar. It operates in Europe, North America and Asia, has several hundred employees, and revenue of roughly 200 million euros. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (GLA1V), with a history linked to the Finnish Tamglass business. B2B equipment maker with little consumer awareness, so its sponsorship relevance is limited.

wiki.title: Glaston
wiki.text: Glaston is a village in the county of Rutland in the East Midlands of England. The population of the civil parish remained unchanged between the 2001 and the 2011 censuses.

about: Formlabs is a Somerville, Massachusetts maker of desktop and industrial 3D printers, best known for the Form series of resin printers (Form 3 and Form 4) and the Fuse series of SLS powder printers, together with materials and PreForm software. Customers include dentists, engineers, designers, manufacturers and universities, and it earns revenue from machines and recurring resin and materials sales. Founded in 2011 by MIT Media Lab alumni, it was valued at about 2 billion dollars in 2021 and has several hundred staff. Private. Well-known B2B brand in 3D printing, with moderate visibility among makers.

wiki.title: Formlabs
wiki.text: Formlabs is a 3D printing technology developer and manufacturer. The Somerville, Massachusetts-based company was founded in September 2011 by three MIT Media Lab students. The company develops and manufactures 3D printers, along with related software and consumables. It raised nearly $3 million in a Kickstarter campaign and created the Form 1, Form 1+, Form 2, Form Cell, Form 3, Form 3L, Form 4, Form 4L, Form Studio 1, and Form Auto stereolithography and Fuse 1, Fuse 1+, and Fuse X1 selective laser sintering 3D printers and accessories.

about: Fictiv is a San Francisco digital manufacturing platform that lets engineers and product teams order custom parts, such as CNC-machined, injection-moulded and 3D-printed components, through an online quote system with a network of vetted factories in the US and Asia. Customers are hardware and robotics companies, automotive, aerospace and medical device firms, paying per order, with software for project management. Founded in 2013 by Dave Evans, it raised about 190 million dollars and was acquired in 2025 by Japanese industrial supplier MISUMI Group. B2B engineering brand with strong recognition among product engineers, none among consumers.
cb_desc: Fictiv is a digital manufacturing and supply chain company tha...

about: Drilling Tools International is a Houston, Texas oilfield services company, listed on Nasdaq (DTI), that rents and sells downhole drilling tools such as drill pipe, stabilisers, motors and specialist equipment to oil and gas operators and drillers, with a growing manufacturing base and a 3D printing capability. Customers are US shale producers and service companies, with some international business. Founded in 1984 and public through a 2023 SPAC merger with ROC Energy Acquisition, it has about 600 employees and revenue of roughly 150 million dollars. Funding of about 41 million dollars. B2B oilfield brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Kuraray
wiki.text: Kuraray Co., Ltd is a Japanese manufacturer of chemicals, fibers and other materials. Their main manufacturing facilities are located in Kurashiki, Okayama. The company's Tokyo administrative offices are located in Otemachi, Chiyoda in the Ote Center Building and its Osaka offices are located in the Umeda Hankyu Building). As of June 2007, Kuraray was the sole worldwide producer of Vectran liquid crystal polymer (LCP) fibre.

about: US digital manufacturer that makes custom prototypes and low-volume parts on demand through its Protolabs and Hubs services, using CNC machining, 3D printing, injection moulding and sheet metal. Listed on the NYSE (PRLB) and based in Maple Plain, Minnesota. Customers are engineers and product developers in medical, automotive, consumer products and aerospace, with revenue around 500 million USD. Well-known B2B brand among engineers.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2008: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Protolabs
wiki.text: Protolabs is a company that provides rapid manufacturing of 3D printed, CNC-machined, sheet metal, and injection-molded custom parts for prototyping and production. Markets like medical devices, aerospace, electronics, appliances, automotive and consumer products use these parts. Protolabs' headquarters are located in Maple Plain, Minnesota, with Minnesota-based manufacturing facilities in Plymouth, Brooklyn Park, and Rosemount, along with additional facilities in Nashua, New Hampshire and Cary, North Carolina. Outside the U.S., the company has manufacturing facilities in England and Germany, in addition to its supplier network of 250 manufac

about: Swarovski is an Austrian maker of precision-cut crystal, selling jewellery, accessories, home decor and Swarovski crystal components, with its own boutiques, e-commerce and wholesale partners worldwide and a business supplying crystal to fashion, watch and lighting brands. Headquartered in Mannedorf, Switzerland (the operations centre is Wattens, Austria); founded 1895 in Wattens. Family-owned. Revenue near 2 billion euros. Strong global consumer brand with luxury-fashion and entertainment tie-ins.

PC Jeweller is an Indian jewellery retailer, headquartered in Delhi, selling gold, diamond and silver jewellery through about 70 showrooms and an online presence. Founded by Padam Chand Gupta and run by his sons, it faced a severe debt crisis from 2018 with lender restructurings, and has since stabilised. Listed on the NSE and BSE (PCJEWELLER). A known regional jewellery brand in northern India, with modest advertising spend.

wiki.title: PC Jeweller
wiki.text: PC Jeweller Limited is a jeweller based in New Delhi, India. It started operations in April 2005 with one showroom at Karol Bagh Delhi and 50 showrooms in India. It is a first generation business promoted by two brothers- Padam Chand Gupta and Balram Garg. It presently has 50 stores in 38 cities across 13 States/UT.

about: BlueStone is a Bengaluru-based Indian online-first fine jewellery brand, founded in 2011, selling certified gold and diamond jewellery through its website and a growing chain of about 275 stores. Revenue is about INR 17bn. Backed by Accel, Kalaari and Iron Pillar, plus Sunil Kant Munjal, it listed on the NSE and BSE in August 2025. Strong online jewellery brand in India with extensive digital advertising.
